text: I have zero technical background, did music in high school ... when Sonnet 3.5 came out. I remember watching a YouTube video building apps using Bolt or Lovable. It basically felt like someone came up to me and said, "You have superpowers now."
speaker: Zevi Arnovitz
context: Lenny introduces Zevi as a product manager with no technical background who has learned to build significant products using AI tools. Zevi explains his background and the moment he discovered AI-powered coding tools. He describes watching a YouTube video about building apps with AI platforms like Bolt or Lovable, which was a transformative moment that made him realize the potential of these new technologies for non-technical people.
text_ko: 저는 기술 배경이 전혀 없고, 고등학교 때 음악을 했어요... Sonnet 3.5가 나왔을 때요. 그때 Bolt나 Lovable을 사용해서 앱 만드는 유튜브 영상을 봤던 기억이 나요. 그 순간 누군가 저한테 "이제 너에게 슈퍼파워가 생겼어."라고 말해준 기분이었어요.
text_zh: 我完全没有技术背景，高中学的是音乐...当Sonnet 3.5发布的时候，我记得看了个YouTube视频，讲怎么用Bolt或者Lovable来开发应用。那感觉就像有人跑过来跟我说："你现在有超能力了。"
text_es: No tengo nada de formación técnica, estudié música en el bachillerato... cuando salió Sonnet 3.5. Me acuerdo de ver un video en YouTube donde construían apps usando Bolt o Lovable. Básicamente fue como si alguien se me hubiera acercado y me dijera: "Ahora tienes súper poderes."
key_sentence: I felt like someone came up to me and said, 'You have superpowers now.'

vocabulary.definition: A technical background refers to a person's education, experience, and skills in technology or related fields. It often includes knowledge of programming, engineering, or other specialized areas.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, having a technical background is often crucial for roles in software development, data analysis, and IT management, as it enables individuals to understand complex systems and contribute effectively to projects.
vocabulary.nuance: While a strong technical background is advantageous, it is not always necessary for success in tech-related roles, as many positions also value creativity and problem-solving skills.

vocabulary.definition: Building apps refers to the process of designing, developing, and deploying software applications for various platforms, including mobile and web. This process involves coding, testing, and user interface design.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech startup ecosystem, building apps is a fundamental activity that drives innovation and product development, often leading to the creation of new business models and revenue streams.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'building apps' implies a hands-on, iterative approach to software development, which can be contrasted with more theoretical or planning-focused discussions.

text: If you're non-technical like me, code is terrifying, but AI just makes it so much possible. In the next coming years, I think everyone's going to become a builder. Titles are going to collapse and responsibilities are going to collapse.
speaker: Zevi Arnovitz
context: Zevi discusses how AI is transforming the ability for non-technical people to build products. He acknowledges that code can be intimidating for those without technical backgrounds, but explains how AI tools have made building applications accessible to everyone. He predicts a future where traditional job titles and role boundaries will become less relevant as AI enables more people to become builders.
text_ko: 저처럼 기술 쪽이 아니면 코드(code)는 정말 무섭게 느껴지는데요, 인공지능(AI)이 그걸 훨씬 가능하게 만들어줘요. 앞으로 몇 년 안에 거의 모든 사람이 빌더(builder)가 될 거라고 생각해요. 직함과 책임의 경계가 무너질 거예요.
text_zh: 像我这样不懂技术的人，一看到代码就头大，但AI让一切都变得可能了。我觉得接下来几年，人人都能成为开发者(builder)。什么职位头衔啊、工作职责划分啊，这些界限都会被打破。
text_es: Si no eres técnico como yo, programar da muchísimo miedo, pero la IA lo hace súper posible. En los próximos años, creo que todo el mundo se va a convertir en creador. Los títulos se van a desdibujar y las responsabilidades también se van a desdibujar.
key_sentence: AI makes it so much possible; everyone's going to become a builder.

vocabulary.definition: Duties or obligations that an individual is accountable for in a given role or position.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, responsibilities outline the expected tasks and functions of an employee, often detailed in job descriptions and performance evaluations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a sense of accountability and can imply varying levels of authority depending on the context, so it is essential to specify the scope of responsibilities when discussing them.

vocabulary.definition: An individual or entity that creates or develops something, particularly in the context of technology or innovation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech environments, a builder is often someone who actively contributes to the creation of products, services, or solutions, emphasizing a hands-on approach to development.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'builder' conveys a sense of proactivity and creativity, and it is often used to inspire collaboration and innovation within teams.

text: It's the best time to be a junior, contrary to what a lot of people are saying, how there's no more junior roles out there.
speaker: Zevi Arnovitz
context: Lenny mentions the common belief that AI will replace people, but those who are better at using AI will have advantages. Zevi responds with an optimistic perspective about opportunities for junior professionals in the AI era. While acknowledging that traditional junior roles may be scarce, he points out the unprecedented opportunity for recent graduates to build startups independently using AI tools.
text_ko: 많은 사람들이 '주니어 자리가 없다'고 말하지만, 오히려 지금이 주니어로 일하기에 가장 좋은 시기예요.
text_zh: 现在做初级反而是最好的时机，和很多人说“已经没有初级岗位（junior roles）了”这个观点恰恰相反。
text_es: Ahora es el mejor momento para los profesionales junior, al contrario de lo que se oye por ahí: que ya no hay puestos junior (roles).
key_sentence: Contrary to what a lot of people are saying, it's the best time to build a startup.
original_text: It's the best time to be a junior, contrary to what a lot of people are saying, how there's no more junior roles out there. Yeah, that's true, but also when else in history could you get out of school and just build a startup on your own?

vocabulary.definition: Opposed in nature, direction, or meaning; inconsistent with something else.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'contrary' is often used to highlight differing opinions or trends, especially when challenging prevailing narratives or assumptions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'contrary' can imply disagreement, it can also suggest a critical perspective that encourages deeper analysis.

text: I created sort of a CTO. So again, I'm not technical. I have been in product for a while, but I know zero stuff about code.
speaker: Zevi Arnovitz
context: Zevi explains his workflow for building products using AI tools. He describes creating a virtual CTO using ChatGPT projects to help with technical decisions and planning. This approach helps him overcome the limitation of coding platforms that immediately start writing code without proper planning, which can lead to bugs and technical issues when building complex features like payment systems.
text_ko: 일종의 최고기술책임자(CTO) 역할을 만든 거예요. 다시 말하지만, 저는 기술 쪽 사람이 아니에요. 프로덕트(product) 쪽에는 꽤 오래 있었지만 코드에 대해서는 전혀 아는 게 없어요.
text_zh: 我算是找了个首席技术官(CTO)。说实话，我不懂技术。我在产品岗待了挺久，但对代码一窍不通。
text_es: Creé algo así como un director de tecnología (CTO). Insisto: no soy técnico. Llevo tiempo en producto, pero no tengo ni idea de código.
key_sentence: I created sort of a CTO, knowing zero stuff about code.
original_text: I created sort of a CTO. So again, I'm not technical. I have been in product for a while, but I know zero stuff about code. So basically what I did was I created a CTO with the custom prompt of it being the complete technical owner of the project.

text: I always think about this where for some reason, the easiest way for me to think about AI is to imagine it as people. And I think ChatGPT would probably be the worst CTO because it's such a people pleaser and it's so sycophantic.
speaker: Zevi Arnovitz
context: Zevi shares his mental framework for working with AI tools effectively. He explains why he customized his AI CTO to be less agreeable than standard ChatGPT, which tends to be overly accommodating. He illustrates this with an example where ChatGPT incorrectly agreed with his comparison between two unrelated technologies, demonstrating the importance of setting up AI to challenge ideas rather than simply agreeing.
text_ko: 저는 왠지 인공지능(AI)을 사람으로 상상하면 생각이 가장 편해요. 그래서 가끔 이렇게 생각해요: ChatGPT는 아마 최악의 최고기술책임자(CTO)가 될 거예요. 사람들 기분 맞춰주느라 지나치게 아첨적이어서 리더로서 냉정한 판단을 하기엔 별로일 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我一直有个想法，不知道为什么，我觉得理解AI最简单的方法就是把它们想象成人。我觉得ChatGPT要是当CTO的话，绝对是最糟糕的，因为它太爱讨好人了，简直就是个马屁精。
text_es: Siempre pienso en esto donde por alguna razón, la forma más fácil para mí de entender la IA es imaginármela como personas. Y creo que ChatGPT sería probablemente el peor CTO del mundo porque es súper complaciente y demasiado adulador.
key_sentence: ChatGPT would be the worst CTO; it's such a people pleaser.

text: start slow with a GPT project, beautiful UI, super simple, then maybe graduate... slowly, slowly, gradually ease in until you open a terminal, go full dark mode, go full dev.
speaker: Zevi Arnovitz
context: Lenny asks about Zevi's progression from ChatGPT projects to advanced coding tools like Cursor. Zevi provides advice for non-technical people who want to start building with AI. He recommends a gradual approach, starting with simple interfaces and slowly progressing to more technical tools, comparing it to exposure therapy for overcoming the fear of code.
text_ko: GPT 프로젝트(GPT project)는 천천히 시작해요. 예쁜 사용자 인터페이스(user interface)로 아주 단순하게 출발하고, 천천히 조금씩 점진적으로 익숙해져요. 준비되면 터미널(terminal)을 열고 다크 모드(dark mode)로 바꾼 다음 본격적으로 개발(dev)에 들어가요.
text_zh: 做 GPT 项目 (GPT project) 先慢点，界面做漂亮、功能超简单，然后再慢慢进阶……一步一步来，逐渐深入，直到有一天你直接打开终端 (terminal)、切到暗黑模式 (dark mode)、完全投入开发 (dev)。
text_es: Empieza despacio con un proyecto GPT: interfaz bonita (UI), súper sencilla. Después, despacio, despacio — ve entrando poco a poco hasta que acabes abriendo una terminal (terminal), activando el modo oscuro (dark mode) y trabajando como desarrollador (dev).
key_sentence: Gradually ease in until you go full dark mode and full dev.
original_text: I would really recommend starting slow with a GPT project, beautiful UI, super simple, then maybe graduate to like a Bolt or a Lovable, and then go to Cursor in light mode, slowly, slowly, gradually ease in until you open a terminal, go full dark mode, go full dev.

vocabulary.definition: In a slow and steady manner, involving small changes over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'gradually' often refers to the incremental implementation of projects or strategies to minimize risk and allow for adjustments.
vocabulary.nuance: This term conveys a sense of patience and careful planning, making it suitable for contexts where rapid change may be detrimental.

vocabulary.definition: To introduce or integrate something gradually or gently, allowing for a smooth transition.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, 'ease in' is commonly used when implementing new technologies or processes, ensuring that team members adapt comfortably without overwhelming them.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase suggests a considerate approach to change, making it appropriate for contexts where user experience and comfort are priorities.

text: What I'll do is basically /review. This tells Claude to start reviewing its own code, but what's even cooler is I have Codex as well as Cursor open. I will have each of them review the code.
speaker: Zevi Arnovitz
context: Lenny mentions that the main challenge for non-technical people using AI to write code is reviewing the code that AI has produced. Zevi explains his solution to this problem: he uses multiple AI models to review each other's code. He has created a workflow where Claude reviews its own code, and then he also uses different AI models like Codex to provide additional code reviews, creating a peer review process.
text_ko: 제가 할 건 기본적으로 /review 명령어(command)를 실행하는 거예요. 이건 Claude에게 자신의 코드를 스스로 리뷰(review)하기 시작하라고 지시하는 건데, 더 멋진 건 Codex와 Cursor도 열어놨다는 점이에요. 각 도구에게 코드 리뷰(code review)를 맡길 거예요.
text_zh: 我要做的基本上就是让它review一下。这样Claude就会开始检查自己的代码，更酷的是我还同时开着Codex和Cursor。我会让它们几个都来检查一遍代码。
text_es: Lo que voy a hacer es básicamente revisar. Esto le dice a Claude que empiece a revisar su propio código, pero lo que está aún más genial es que tengo Codex y también Cursor abiertos. Voy a hacer que cada uno de ellos revise el código.
key_sentence: What's even cooler is having each of them review the code.

vocabulary.definition: To examine or assess something critically in order to provide feedback or make improvements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, reviews are often conducted on projects, code, or performance to ensure quality and identify areas for enhancement.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'review' implies a thorough examination, it can also suggest a formal process, making it suitable for structured evaluations rather than casual observations.
